summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 8.9% YoY to INR597 crore with PAT up 39% to INR108 crore; FY27 revenue guided at minimum INR2,500 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest quarter, with revenue of INR597 crore (up 8.9% YoY), EBITDA of INR157 crore (up 29%, margin 26.2%) and PAT of INR108 crore (up 39%). Full-year FY26 revenue was flat at about INR2,120 crore, as the 50% additional US tariff hit the first nine months (nine-month performance about 10% below FY25), while EBITDA was INR500 crore and PAT INR338 crore. Management said the business was debt-free with INR774 crore of cash and liquid investments, and announced an additional INR191 crore sun control line. Guidance for FY27 is a minimum of INR2,500 crore revenue with a 25% (plus/minus 2%) margin band, though the call gave no explicit EBITDA margin number.

financial_highlights.change: Flat vs FY25 per analyst; company cites highest-ever revenue

segments.name: Sun control films (SCF)
segments.commentary: About 50% of FY26 revenue. Lines running at 75-80% utilisation; management expects full utilisation by about Q2 FY28 at 15-20% growth. Architectural is about 25% of SCF sales and growing 25-30%.

segments.name: Paint protection films (PPF)
segments.commentary: About 25% of FY26 revenue. Running at 85-89% utilisation with full order books. Four OEM direct partnerships in India (including a Mahindra tie-up), two more under discussion.

segments.name: Commodity / IPD products
segments.commentary: About 25% of FY26 revenue, per management's split.

segments.name: Garware Home Solutions (GHS) and D2C
segments.commentary: D2C is about 10-15% of overall revenue (about 40% in India). Six GHS studios operational, target 50 by end FY27, and FY28 target above INR200 crore across GHS and new products like PDLC.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue minimum INR2,500 crore, with growth of about 20% CAGR cited as the long-run track record; management said guidance is 25% plus/minus 2% (previously plus/minus 3%), read as a margin/growth band.
New sun control line (INR191 crore, about 1,200 lakh sq ft capacity, robotics-enabled) commercial production expected by June 2027 (Q1 FY28), at the same location.
TPU backward-integration line expected to commission by October 2026; first TPU products (automotive and architectural) to start sales in Q3 FY27 with minimal revenue initially.
Middle East (MENA) sales about $15 million currently, targeting $20-22 million this year (25-30% CAGR).
Management expects margin improvement once the TPU line is on stream; no explicit margin number given.
Global Application Studios and D2C target 25% then 35% of business volume over time, which management says will lift margins; D2C margins 25-30% above distributor margins.
risks_watch: Customer in-house PPF manufacturing plan; management says there is no direct volume impact but this is a key PPF exposure.
US automotive sales decline (5-6%) and tariff uncertainty on US demand.
Refund of US tariffs is uncertain and accounting treatment unclear; some amounts may need to be passed to customers.
Raw material cost inflation (PTA, MEG, crude linkage) and the pace of pass-through to consumer products.
Capacity constraint risk: SCF near full utilisation by FY28 and PPF at 85-89%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q4 and the outlook, with a clear focus on D2C and new products. Evasive on the current-quarter volume trend (April), on tariff refund amounts and on partnership status with Chinese players, citing confidentiality and accounting.
key_quotes: So we expect minimum INR2,500 crores revenue for FY '27, right?
We are confident of scaling this to 50 studios by the end of FY '27.
Even after these investments, our balance sheet remains strong and debt -free with a cash reserves of INR774 crores

qa_highlights.question: Split of FY26 revenue across sun control films, PPF and commodity products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% from sun control films and 25% each from PPF and IPD products.

qa_highlights.question: Why build a new SCF line ahead of another PPF line when PPF is at 85-89% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SCF demand is growing fastest, architectural and GHS add demand, and an SCF line (about 125 lakh sq ft/month) can be used for fungible PPF output (about 25 lakh sq ft/month per PPF line), with PPF expected to reach full utilisation by next year.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Chinese partnerships and OEM tie-ups in PPF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said four OEM direct partnerships are in the books (including Mahindra & Mahindra), two more are under discussion, and the Chinese partnership talks are still ongoing and not concluded.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk from a large PPF customer setting up in-house manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct impact as the company is not the sole supplier, and the product's nano dispersion and adhesive technology is unique, so volumes are not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East subsidiary status and sales outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MENA sales are about $15 million, targeting $20-22 million this year at 25-30% CAGR, with the subsidiary completed and some local value addition work under way.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the US tariff now versus earlier, and what is the refund outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the base tariff is 6.26% and the additional tariff is now 10% versus 50% last year; the refund is expected but not guaranteed and the accounting treatment is still to be determined, so no amount was given.

capex_capacity: New sun control film (SCF) line: INR191 crore investment, about 1,200 lakh sq ft capacity, robotics and automation; entirely new facility at the same location, adjacent to existing line; commercial production by June 2027 (Q1 FY28).
SCF lines at 75-80% utilisation; management expects these to be fully utilised by about Q2 FY28 (described on the call as 'by next year') at 15-20% growth; debottlenecking of old plants possible.
PPF lines at 85-89% utilisation with full order books; management plans to use fungibility of the new SCF line to add PPF output, with a further PPF line to be considered later.
TPU backward-integration line expected to commission by October 2026; first TPU products (automotive and architectural) to begin sales in Q3 FY27 with minimal initial revenue.
Over the last few years, over INR500 crore spent on capacity across 2 PPF lines, 1 SCF line, metalizer and 1 TPU line, funded entirely from internal accruals.
Per-line output cited: PPF line about 25 lakh sq ft/month vs SCF line about 125 lakh sq ft/month; new SCF line described as roughly 30% capacity addition.
demand_pricing: FY26 revenue mix: sun control films about 50%, PPF about 25%, IPD/commodity about 25%. Architectural is about 25% of SCF sales and growing 25-30%.

Management guides FY27 revenue of minimum INR2,500 crore and 25% plus/minus 2% margin band (previously plus/minus 3%); 9M FY26 was about 10% below FY25, and the company cites about 20% CAGR over the last four years excluding FY26.
US share of revenue: about 48% in FY25, about 45% in FY26. MENA sales about $15 million (roughly 6% of revenue), targeting $20-22 million this year at 25-30% CAGR.

D2C is about 10-15% of overall revenue (about 40% in India). Management targets 25% then 35% of business volume through Global Application Studios and D2C, with D2C margins 25-30% above distributor margins.

Brand mix: about 55% sold under Garware/Global brands and 40-45% to private labels (direct or neutral). Raw material pass-through: industrial products closely linked to PTA/MEG; SCF price increase passed on for many customers; management says no negative impact from raw material inflation.

US inventory in transit plus warehousing about 16 million (currency unspecified). Garware Home Solutions: 6 studios operational, target 50 by end FY27; FY28 target above INR200 crore across GHS and new products such as PDLC.
Q1 described as seasonally strong for exports (June-September) and India (up to June); April and May cited as ordering months for exports.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at minimum INR2,500 crore (about 18% above FY26's ~INR2,120 crore), backed by a INR191 crore sun control line due June 2027, SCF lines at 75-80% and PPF at 85-89% utilisation with full order books, and a TPU line commissioning by October 2026; the new capacity lands only in Q1 FY28, so most FY27 growth must come from existing lines and demand.
